title: Derived morphism sheaves evaluate on weakly contractible pro-etale affines
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $B$ a finite commutative ring, and $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $E\in D(B)$ be bounded with finite $B$-module cohomology, and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ be bounded with finite locally constant cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\underline E$ for its constant sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define $\mathcal H_{E,K}$ and $\mathcal I_{E,K}$ by sheafifying, on the etale site, the presheaves $V\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ and $V\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{D(V_{\mathrm{et}},B)}(\underline E|_V,K|_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For every affine object $U\to X$ weakly contractible for $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is surjective on sections over $U$, there are canonical bijections
$$
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal H_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U),\qquad
 (\nu_X^*\mathcal I_{E,K})(U)\cong\operatorname{Isom}_{D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)}(\underline E|_U,(\nu_X^*K)|_U).
$$
Here restriction is to the localized pro-etale site over $U$, identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$. The bijections extend pullback of actual etale-local morphisms, preserve identity morphisms and composition whenever defined, and are natural in $E,K$ and restriction between such objects. For a homomorphism $B\to C$ of finite commutative rings for which $E_C=E\otimes_B^L C$ and $K_C=K\otimes_B^L C$ remain bounded with the corresponding finite cohomology hypotheses, they commute with derived scalar extension: the map of pulled-back morphism or isomorphism sheaves induced by $f\mapsto f\otimes_B^L C$ evaluates to the same operation on actual derived morphisms. No finite Tor dimension is assumed.

proof.text: $B$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a finite set and hence generated by its elements. The bounded finite cohomology hypothesis and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] make $E$ pseudo-coherent. By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] choose a bounded-above finite-free representative $P$ of $E$, zero above $b$. Choose a representative $N$ of $K$ zero below some $a$, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Applying the constant-sheaf functor to $P$ represents $\underline E$: constant presheaves preserve kernels, and set sheafification preserves finite limits, hence the underlying constant-sheaf functor preserves kernels. For a surjection of coefficient modules, its underlying set map is the coequalizer of the two projections of its kernel pair: a function constant on the fibres factors uniquely through the quotient. Constant presheaves preserve this sectionwise coequalizer. Set sheafification, being a left adjoint by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], preserves that coequalizer and hence gives an epimorphism of underlying sheaves of sets; finite-limit preservation identifies its sheafified kernel pair. Thus the induced map of constant module sheaves is an epimorphism. Applying the induced addition and $B$-action gives exactness on constant module sheaves, so cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms are preserved. Exact restriction and exact $\nu_X^*$ preserve these representatives and bounds. We do not shorten $P$ to a perfect complex. The coefficient and constant-object identifications under geometric inverse image follow as well: a constant sheaf of sets is the coproduct of copies of the final sheaf indexed by its elements (sheafify the identical description of the constant presheaf); the inverse image is a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint, so preserves this coproduct and final object, together with the induced module operations.

proof.text:
Put $M=R\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(\underline E,K)$ on the etale site. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] to $(\underline P,N)$. Its degree-$n$ model $T$ has only the indices $a-n\leq i\leq b$. For $P^i=B^{r_i}$, the sheaf-Hom definition identifies $\mathcal Hom(\underline{P^i},N^{i+n})$ with $(N^{i+n})^{r_i}$: a map is determined by the images of the $r_i$ standard basis vectors. The same formula holds after any slice restriction or $
u_X^*$. These functors preserve finite products, and exactness preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. The matrices of $d_P$ and the maps $d_N$ give exactly the same differential $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$ on both sides. Applying the same model theorem on the pro-etale site therefore gives the canonical comparison $
u_X^*M\simeq R\mathcal Hom(\underline E,
u_X^*K)$. On slices its restriction is the derived internal Hom of the restricted objects, by this same termwise calculation. The model vanishes for $n<a-b$, so it is bounded below even though $P$ may be unbounded to the left.

proof.text:
On every etale slice, [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies the morphism presheaf with $V\mapsto H^0(V,M)$, by step 2. Choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $M$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $J|_V$ remains K-injective, so this presheaf is $V\mapsto\ker(J^0(V)	o J^1(V))/\operatorname{im}(J^{-1}(V)	o J^0(V))$. Sheafify this kernel-image quotient. Exact module sheafification sends its kernel and image to the sheaf kernel and image and fixes each already-sheaf term $J^i$. The result is precisely $\ker(d_J^0)/\operatorname{im}(d_J^{-1})=H^0(M)$. This proves the identification $\mathcal H_{E,K}=H^0(M)$ directly (the elementary kernel-quotient calculation of Tag 0BKV), naturally in $M$. Exact $
u_X^*$ gives $
u_X^*\mathcal H_{E,K}\simeq H^0(
u_X^*M)$. These canonical maps extend actual etale-local pullback: the global-Hom formula sends a derived map to its internal-Hom class, and the kernel-quotient map sends that class to its cohomology-sheaf section. All maps arise from these same representatives and the induced localization functors.

proof.text:
Evaluation over the weakly contractible $U$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits]. In a resolution $
u_X^*M	o J$ used to compute derived sections, evaluation preserves the quasi-isomorphism: exactness makes its evaluated cohomology equal to evaluated sheaf cohomology. Consequently $H^0(R\Gamma(U,
u_X^*M))=H^0(
u_X^*M)(U)$. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on the slice and the model's slice calculation to identify the left side with the actual derived Hom in the first displayed bijection. The site and coefficient identification with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], since $U$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. This proves the Hom bijection.

source.place: Tags 08JI, 0BKV, 0946; agent assembly with proetale comparison

proof.text: For the isomorphism assertion also form the morphism sheaves for $(K,\underline E)$, $(K,K)$ and $(\underline E,\underline E)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-derived-local-constancy], etale locally $K$ has a bounded finite coefficient model. The calculation of steps 1-3 therefore applies on this covering to each pair, giving the same comparison of morphism sheaves for all four pairs. The local finite-diagonal comparisons agree on overlaps because they are the canonical comparisons induced by pullback of morphisms, so they identify the pulled-back etale morphism sheaves with the degree-zero cohomology sheaves of the four pro-etale derived internal Homs. To evaluate these on $U$, work now entirely on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$: for any pair $(A,D)$ among the four pulled-back pairs, choose a complex $L$ representing $A$ and a K-injective representative $J$ of $D$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], its derived internal Hom is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L,J)$. Restriction of $J$ remains K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. For an object $V\to U$, the slice-Hom formula reads $\mathcal Hom(L^i,J^{i+n})(V)=\operatorname{Hom}(L^i|_V,J^{i+n}|_V)$ on the pro-etale site and its slice at $U$; products are sectionwise, so restriction identifies every degree and the differential $d_Jf-(-1)^nf d_L$ of this complex with $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L|_U,J|_U)$. The derived internal Hom definition therefore identifies its restriction with the derived internal Hom on the slice. [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] and exact evaluation as in step 4 give the actual Hom comparison on $U$ for each pair. Composition and identities commute with these comparisons: the presheaf maps are induced by the functor on localized derived categories; their degree-zero classes and sheafification give the same compositions, and exact evaluation passes these classes to the same global morphisms. Now the isomorphism presheaf is the set of pairs $(f,h)$ satisfying $hf=1_{\underline E}$ and $fh=1_K$, projected to $f$. The inverse is unique, since $h=h(fh')=(hf)h'=h'$. Sheafification preserves this finite-limit description by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], as do geometric inverse image and section evaluation. Applying the four Hom comparisons gives precisely pairs of actual inverse derived maps. This proves the Isom bijection and the identity and composition clauses.

Naturality in the two variables and slice restriction follows from the canonical map taking an actual derived morphism to its internal-Hom class: precomposition, postcomposition and restriction act on that same map, and the identifications above commute with them. For $B	o C$ as in the statement, the derived tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies $
u_X^*(F\otimes_B^L C)$ with $(
u_X^*F)\otimes_B^L C$, naturally in $F$ and therefore in actual derived maps $f$. Thus on localized etale morphisms the two routes send $f$ to the very same map $(
u_X^*f)\otimes_B^L C$. Sheafify this equality; the canonical actual-morphism-to-sheaf-class maps on the pro-etale site respect the tensor functor, so the resulting square of morphism sheaves commutes. Evaluation on $U$ and the Hom bijections already proved identify its bottom map with actual derived scalar extension. The inverse-pair description of step 5 gives the same square for Isom, since a functor carries inverse pairs to inverse pairs. Apply the Hom computation over $C$ using the assumed boundedness of $E_C,K_C$; do not tensor the $B$-Hom complex to claim a base-change isomorphism for internal Hom. No Tor-dimension assumption is used.

split_report.summary: Proved the bridge via bounded-above finite-free models and bounded-below targets (08JI), the explicit kernel-image sheafification calculation (0BKV), exact pro-etale inverse image and weakly contractible evaluation. Isom is a finite-limit inverse-pair construction; scalar extension uses natural tensor pullback, not a false internal-Hom base-change isomorphism. Added one generic statement-only tool; kept the original statement.

tool_uses.why: K-injective restriction on any ringed-site slice supplies the resolutions used in steps 3 and 5; this unit has no slice-resolution substitute.
Global derived Hom is hypercohomology of internal Hom, applied on the two sites and their slices; this is generic ringed-site infrastructure absent from this unit.
Exact restriction preserves representatives and quasi-isomorphisms on slices; this unit has no replacement for that foundational operation.
Identifies the site slice at an arbitrary weakly etale object with its own pro-etale site and constant coefficients; this unit has no such localization theorem.
Supplies K-injective representatives of arbitrary complexes of module sheaves on small ringed sites; this unit has no resolution-existence theorem.
